topics.title: Simon lashes Mexico's Pacific coast
topics.summary: Hurricane Simon pounded Mexico's Pacific coast as a powerful Category 4 storm, bringing dangerous winds, flooding risk and disruption near Puerto Vallarta and nearby coastal towns.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a beach trip suddenly turns into storm prep, who gets practical first and who keeps refreshing the forecast like it owes them answers?

topics.title: Isaias cleanup shifts inland
topics.summary: After hitting Florida and Alabama, Isaias' remnants pushed heavy rain toward Appalachia and the mid-Atlantic, keeping flood worries alive as crews worked on power and road cleanup.
topics.discussionPrompt: When the worst of a storm has passed but the errands are still a mess, who becomes the neighborhood logistics captain?

topics.title: Trump cites Ukraine energy ceasefire
topics.summary: President Trump said Russia and Ukraine had reached an energy ceasefire, though he offered few details and Ukrainian diplomacy remained under close scrutiny.
topics.discussionPrompt: When someone announces a big deal without much fine print, who celebrates early and who immediately asks where the paperwork is?

topics.title: Saudi Arabia heightens airport alert
topics.summary: Saudi Arabia remained on alert after strikes around Riyadh's airport, while Middle East diplomacy and regional security concerns continued to shift quickly.
topics.discussionPrompt: When travel plans depend on fast-changing security news, who calmly waits for updates and who starts building three backup itineraries?
sourceNames: NPR News Now via Podcast Rex

topics.title: DOJ reviews White House TV pool dispute
topics.summary: The Justice Department said it is investigating whether a halt in White House TV pool coverage violated antitrust law, extending a fight over press access.
topics.discussionPrompt: If covering an event turns into a rulebook argument, who defends the process and who just wants cameras back in the room?

topics.title: AI self-policing debate grows
topics.summary: San Francisco Tech Week put AI oversight back in the spotlight, with founders welcoming lighter federal regulation while critics questioned voluntary safety commitments.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a fast-moving industry says it can grade its own homework, who trusts the ambition and who asks for a red pen?

topics.title: Guardian highlights UK identity study
topics.summary: A new report covered by The Guardian says visible Christian nationalism in Britain may be driven largely by people who seldom attend church.
topics.discussionPrompt: When symbols mean different things to different people, who sees tradition and who sees politics sneaking into the room?

topics.title: Guardians complete playoff comeback
topics.summary: Cleveland beat the White Sox in Game 5, completing an ALDS comeback from two games down behind a dominant Gavin Williams pitching performance.
topics.discussionPrompt: After a team digs out of a 2-0 hole, who calls it destiny and who insists the bullpen spreadsheet explains everything?

topics.title: Kipchoge wins Melbourne Marathon
topics.summary: Eliud Kipchoge won his first marathon in three years, breaking the Melbourne Marathon record and saying his body is still peaking.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a legend says they are still peaking, who gets inspired and who suddenly feels judged by their unused running shoes?

topics.title: Streaming week mixes music and games
topics.summary: AP's weekly entertainment picks spotlight new releases from Katseye, Marvel's VisionQuest, a Tenzing Norgay drama and a new Castlevania game.
topics.discussionPrompt: When the watchlist and game backlog both expand at once, who makes a schedule and who samples everything for five minutes?
